entries.title: CLI update: block-operations

acceptedPr.title: perf(cli): scan only the tag seam when appending stream text
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## What

The text streaming path in `cli/src/utils/block-operations.ts` concatenated the whole accumulated block with each incoming delta and then ran two `String.includes` scans over the result:

```ts
const combinedText = lastBlock.content + text
if (combinedText.includes(THINK_OPEN_TAG) || combinedText.includes(THINK_CLOSE_TAG)) { ... }
```

That made one reply cost **O(n²) in its own length** — every delta re-walked everything before it, allocating and flattening the concatenation each time.

## Why it's safe to narrow the scan

A think tag can only be *completed* by the delta that completes it, at the seam between the block's tail and that delta. A tag already sitting inside the block was split out when it arrived. So the check now:

1. looks at the last 7 characters of the block (the widest partial tag, `</think`), plus the delta itself;
2. falls back to the original full-block scan whenever either contains `<`.

`<` in ordinary prose (`a < b`) still takes the full path, so nothing is lost.

## Measurement (`bun`, same machine, before → after)

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 8,000 deltas, 470 KB, plain text | 434 ms | **1.1 ms** |
| 4,000 deltas, 234 KB | 117 ms | **0.9 ms** |
| 2,000 deltas, 117 KB | 34 ms | **0.7 ms** |
| 1,000 deltas, 59 KB | 21 ms | **0.4 ms** |
| 8 subagents × 600 deltas | 38 ms | **5.5 ms** |

Cost is now linear in stream length instead of quadratic (`us/delta` was rising 17 → 54 as the stream grew; it now sits flat below 0.5).

Memory: no leak found on this path. The batched updater's interval is already disposed when a turn ends (`use-send-message.ts`), so it was not changed.

## Verification

- **Behavioural equivalence, not just tests:** 432 corpus scenarios (18 texts × 12 chunk sizes, root and agent paths) dumped from both implementations — **byte-identical** output, sha256 `6e06dde1…`.
- `bun test src/utils src/hooks` — **2672 pass, 0 fail** (157 files).
- `bun run typecheck` — exit 0.
- New `block-operations-streaming.test.ts` covers tags split inside the tag syntax at every seam position, the 7-char `</think` boundary, and long blocks keeping every character.

One pre-existing quirk surfaced while writing the tests and is left untouched: `<think></think>` with no content emits zero blocks, and a tag arriving after a long prefix folds the prefix into the reasoning block. Both behave identically before and after this change, hence the narrower assertions in the new test file.

acceptedPr.title: cli: render the first frame before the terminal probe and keychain answer
acceptedPr.author: Salhi-zh
acceptedPr.body:
## What

Startup awaited two IPC-bound operations before the renderer existed:

1. `detectTerminalTheme()` — a pair of OSC 10/11 queries bounded by a 2 s global timeout. Terminals that swallow OSC queries (misconfigured tmux, some SSH muxes) burned the whole 2 s before a single frame painted; even responsive terminals paid tens-to-hundreds of ms.
2. `loadStoredAuthToken()` — an OS keychain round trip, ahead of `parseArgs`/registry/renderer work that never reads the token.

## Change

**Theme:** the OSC probe now starts *in the background* — still **before** `createCliRenderer()`, so its stdin data listener attaches first and the reply is consumed as the probe answer rather than stray keystrokes. The first frame resolves from the synchronous evidence (`COLORFGBG`, `TERM_BACKGROUND`, per-terminal hints, gated on "no query was sent" so a hint can never pre-empt a real answer). When the answer lands it is applied through the **existing live re-theme path** the theme file watchers and SIGUSR2 use. Settled state is identical to the old ordering whenever the terminal answers: the OSC slot wins over the env evidence by the same detector priority, and probe semantics (two queries, per-query + global timeouts, swallow→null) are untouched. A fallback await before renderer creation restores the old wait only when there was nothing to overlap, still deadline-bounded.

**Keychain:** overlapped with `parseArgs`, the agent/skill registries, and renderer staging; awaited only where a decision is actually published (login/publish branches, launch/crash analytics rows) plus a bounded fallback pre-renderer. Every other consumer reads post-paint.

**Resume path bonus:** `getMostRecentChatDir` statted every chat dir twice (mtime, then `isDirectory()` in a filter type-guard) — now one `withFileTypes` pass, one stat per dir, half the syscalls on the `--continue` scan.

## Tests

New coverage pins the ordering contract: env value resolvable on the first frame, pre-init OSC answers picked up by the initial resolve, post-paint answers applied via live re-theme, same-theme settles are no-ops. Full cli suite: **4343 pass / 41 skip / 0 fail**, typecheck clean.

It adds `cli/src/utils/preload-guard.ts` to detect and report foreign preload injections, and lowers `MESSAGE_BATCH_SIZE` in `cli/src/hooks/use-chat-messages.ts` from 15 to 6.

ai.title: Mark host continuation prompts so they never count as an idle return
ai.summary: The agent runtime now tags a host-written prompt that carries on work the user already asked for (a drained turn's resume, an automatic follow-up pass) so it never counts as the user returning after an idle gap. The SDK exposes the `promptIsContinuation` boolean on `RunOptions` and the runtime uses it to attach `CONTINUATION_PROMPT_TAG` to the user prompt message and to record `continuation_prompt: 'true'` in the compaction correlation telemetry that Axiom reads. Subagent spawns explicitly set the flag to false because a subagent's prompt is its parent's request, not a host resume. Three other files are touched: the shared Axiom allowlist gains the `continuation_prompt` field, `spawn-agent-utils.ts` forces the flag to false for subagents, and the SDK's `runOnce` destructures and forwards the flag to `callMainPrompt`.

eli5.text: The development team tightened the internal security checks and health diagnostics by hiding several helper tools from other parts of the system, ensuring they are only used exactly where intended. This change is internal maintenance that does not alter any visible features, settings, or the daily experience of using the assistant. You will not notice any difference in how the software works or what you can do with it.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.2.36 releases DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Slow presets and CLI
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release 0.2.36 replaces MiMo v2.6 Flash Slow with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Slow in the limited-tier model picker presets because MiMo's provider is down and its rows are served by DeepSeek, as noted in the product comment dated 2026-11-03. The release also defers the terminal color probe and OS keychain read to the background so the first frame paints immediately using synchronous environment evidence. Additionally, the agent runtime removes the `evaluateCompactionTrigger` function and tags continuation prompts with `CONTINUATION_PROMPT_TAG` to prevent them from counting as idle returns.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/util/freebuff-model-presets.ts`, the `getFreebuffModelPresets` function was modified to replace `FREEBUFF_MIMO_SLOW_CATALOG_KEY` with `FREEBUFF_DEEPSEEK_SLOW_CATALOG_KEY` in the premium ladder, with a comment stating "MiMo's provider is down and its rows are served by DeepSeek, so the ladders that led on MiMo v2.6 Flash Slow... now lead on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Slow."
ai.unknowns: The specific mechanism by which MiMo's provider being down causes DeepSeek to serve its rows is not detailed in the diff, only stated in the product comment.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.2.36 updates the free model selection logic to steer users toward DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Slow, replacing previous recommendations centered on MiMo v2.6 Flash Slow because that model's provider is currently unavailable. The terminal interface now loads visual themes in the background instead of waiting for the terminal to report its colors, which allows the first screen to appear immediately while the correct dark or light mode is applied shortly after. A new safety check warns if external code attempts to inject itself into the Freebuff process before startup, though this warning does not currently stop the program from running. Conversation history management was refined so that automatic follow-up prompts do not trigger unnecessary background summarization tasks. Additionally, the release introduces pricing and plan update logic for accounts created on or after November 3, 2026, which receive reduced monthly credits immediately, while older subscribers retain their previous rates until a specific date in November 2026.

facts: Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Slow, Muse Spark 1.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast in view, every other Premium and Powerful row under Show more. The rows being retired carry an Ending pill (default-config.ts); accounts created from 2026-11-03 get their own cut-down set (new-account-catalog.ts).
Standard, last in the picker: the same rows in the same places as the limited layout (default-config.ts's `LIMITED_LAYOUT`), so every viewer sees one Standard set (product, 2026-11-03, Victor).
Powerful: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Fast first and in view (25, or 50 in DeepSeek's peak window), then cheapest to dearest under Show more.
